symptom: ako/mxcli#1340 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1483): "`mxcli run --local` sometimes stops for more than 10 minutes, without any output, at: `Resolving 4 managed Java dependency/dependencies (...)...` ... The same happened in the first build of `mxcli new` (step 6)." Each `mx sync-java-dependencies` left a Gradle 8.5 daemon running for hours; the hang coincided with an idle daemon from an earlier run, and `GRADLE_OPTS=-Dorg.gradle.daemon=false` made the sync finish in ~12s with nothing left behind (Windows 11, Mendix 11.12.4)
cause: `SyncJavaDependencies` ran `cmd.Run()` with no bound and no progress (the #1396 WaitDelay only covers the pipe AFTER mx exits, not an mx that never does), and every one-shot mx/mxbuild run (sync, `mxcli new`'s settle build, docker build) used Gradle's default daemon, which outlives the run and is what the next run attached to
insight: Three Gradle-daemon findings now (#1396 pipe held after exit, the 2026-10-11 unbounded mxbuild, this one) are one lesson: a one-shot that runs Gradle must neither leave a daemon nor wait on one unbounded — bound the tree with the existing watchdog and turn the daemon off, rather than patching each symptom. The cheap tell in the report was 'Mendix's own mx sync on the same project took 6-12s': same tool, different state, so the state (a daemon) was the cause, not mxcli's arguments. APPEND to GRADLE_OPTS — clobbering it drops a proxy, which on a proxied host turns into mx's misleading 'Failed to find some hosts' (sibling finding #1450) — and leave an explicit org.gradle.daemon alone; on Windows compare the key case-insensitively, or a second GRADLE_OPTS beside 'Gradle_Opts' replaces the user's value. Measured with real Gradle 8.14.3 here: GRADLE_OPTS='-Xmx256m -Dorg.gradle.daemon=false' gradle help -> 'No Gradle daemons are running'; plain gradle help -> one IDLE daemon left. No Mendix mx on this host, so the mx/mxbuild side rests on the reporter's measurement. `mxbuild --serve` deliberately keeps its daemon (it builds per change). Tests are fast with a fake mx that prints then `sleep 30` and an env-injected 700ms bound; revert proof: bare cmd.Run() blocks past the 15s guard with empty output, and the env tests show GRADLE_OPTS unchanged
